informal: The Lean defines the finite correction iteration \(E_t\), the pilot that chooses the column multiplier \(\gamma(V)\) by detector expectations, the residual \(D=C-E+EC\) and the copy step \(C^+\), proves the factorial truncation, pilot, detector, residual and copy bounds, and shows that the reward identity \(v=W+Cv\) is preserved so that \(W_k\) approaches \(v\) within \(|S|2^kb_{i+k}\).

results.informal: For every multiplier \(0\le g\le1\), the iterates \(E_t\) of \(E_t=fQ((C+E_{t-1}C)/f)g\) increase in \(t\), consecutive differences satisfy \(\Delta_{t+1}\le5\,\Delta_tC\), and \(E_{T+1}(x,y)-E_T(x,y)\le f(5/A)^T/T!\).
results.note: Lean never forms the fixed point \(E_*\); it proves the factorial bound directly for the consecutive differences \(E_{T+1}-E_T\) with \(\theta_1=A=1/4096\) and \(L_Q=5\), by the same row-support counting argument as the paper.

decls.name: factorial
decls.informal: If \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions at rate \(f>0\) and \(0\le g\le1\), then for all \(T,x,y\), \(E_{T+1}(x,y)-E_T(x,y)\le f\,(5/A)^T/T!\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.factorial/0: Let \(R=C-E_{T+1}+E_{T+1}C\) and \(A_x=\{y:E_{T+1}(x,y)>0\}\); \(R\) is nonnegative substochastic and \(R(x,y)\ge Af\) on \(A_x\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.factorial/4: By induction on \(t\le T\), \(\Delta_t(x,y)\le f(5f)^t\binom{|\{z\in A_x:z<y\}|}{t}\), since in \(\Delta_{t+1}\le5\Delta_tC\) only intermediate vertices \(z\in A_x\) with \(z<y\) contribute.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.factorial/5: Apply this at \(t=T\) and put \(m=|\{z\in A_x:z<y\}|\).

decls.name: transfer_diff
decls.informal: If \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions, \(f>0\) and \(0\le g\le1\), then \(\Delta_{n+1}(x,y)\le5\,(\Delta_nC)(x,y)\) where \(\Delta_n=E_{n+1}-E_n\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.transfer_diff/6: Restate the goal in terms of \(h_{n+1}\).

decls.name: mono_steps
decls.informal: If \(f>0\), \(0\le g\le1\) and \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions, then \(t\mapsto E_t\) is monotone: \(E_0\le E_1\le E_2\le\cdots\).

results.informal: For the pilot corrections \(\widehat E_k\) and actual corrections \(E_k\): both are nonnegative, strictly forward, supported in the active set, with entries \(\le kf\) and row sums \(\le k\); and \(E_k\le\widehat E_k\) for \(k\le k_*\).
results.note: The predicate SB with constant \(k\) is exactly the paper's list (nonnegative, entries \(\le kf\), rows \(\le k\), forward support in the active set), and cpilot is \(E_k\le\widehat E_k\); the pilot inputs \(G_i\) are covered by the companion lemma tbounds.

decls.name: pilot_bounds
decls.informal: If \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions with support in \(S'\), then for every \(k\) the pilot correction \(\widehat E_k\) satisfies \(E\ge0\), \(E(x,y)\le kf\), \(E\mathbf 1\le k\mathbf 1\), and every positive entry has \(x<y\) in the active set \(S'\).

decls.name: cpilot
decls.informal: If \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions and \(k\le k_*\), then \(E_k\le\widehat E_k\).

decls.name: cbounds
decls.informal: If \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions with support in \(S'\), then for every \(k\) the actual correction \(E_k\) satisfies \(E\ge0\), \(E(x,y)\le kf\), \(E\mathbf 1\le k\mathbf 1\), and every positive entry has \(x<y\) in the active set \(S'\).

results.informal: If at least \((128+4(J+1))/b_l\) rows \(x\) have \(G(x,y)\ge2\delta b_l\) then \(U(y)\ge9/10\); always \((J+1)U(y)\le\#\{x:G(x,y)>\delta b_l\}\pi_{b_l}\); and a positive multiplier \(\gamma(V_{k+1}(y))>0\) forces \(\#\{x:G_k(x,y)\ge2\delta f\}\cdot f\le128+4(J+1)\).
results.note: These three lemmas are the three bullet points of the paper lemma with the concrete thresholds \(\delta_1=2\delta\), \(\delta_0=\delta\), \(R_*=128+4(J+1)\), proved by the same second-moment and row-gate arguments.

decls.name: U_heavy
decls.informal: If \(S\) is admissible, \(G\) satisfies the bounds with constant \(k\) at rate \(b_l\), \(2^l\le P\), \((1+32k/\eta(\delta))\cdot128\le K+1\) and \(128+4(J+1)\le\#\{x:G(x,y)\ge2\delta b_l\}\cdot b_l\), then \(U(y)\ge9/10\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_heavy/0: Let \(W=\{x:G(x,y)\ge2\delta b_l\}\), \(z_i\) the indicator that the row gate of \(i\) is not full, \(T(s)\) the number of retained rows of \(W\), and \(m=|W|\pi_{b_l}\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_heavy/4: Let \(\text{loss}(s,t)\) be the number of retained rows of \(W\) whose gate fails, and \(v(s,t)\) the detector score.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_heavy/5/0: Let \(B\) be the retained rows of \(W\) and \(S_0\subseteq B\) those with a full row gate.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_heavy/5/8/1: Every row of \(S_0\) has mark \(1\), so the \(J\)th largest mark is at least \(1\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_heavy/5/9: In all cases the inequality holds.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_heavy/9/1/0: Each row gate fails with conditional probability at most \(1/128\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_heavy/9/1/1: Sum this over the \(T(s)\) retained rows.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_heavy/10: Average the pointwise inequality over \(s\) and \(t\).

decls.name: U_light
decls.informal: \((J+1)\,U(y)\le\#\{x:G(x,y)>\delta b_l\}\cdot\pi_{b_l}\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/0: For all \(s,t\), \((J+1)\,\text{score}(s,t)\) is at most the number of retained rows \(x\) with \(G(x,y)>\delta b_l\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/0/0: The score lies in \([0,1]\); split into the cases score \(=0\) and score \(>0\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/0/1: If the score is \(0\) the bound is trivial.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/0/2: If the score is positive, more than \(J\) retained rows have a positive mark.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/0/3: Hence more than \(J\) retained rows satisfy \(G(x,y)>\delta b_l\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/0/3/0: It suffices that each retained row with positive mark has \(G(x,y)>\delta b_l\); suppose instead \(G(x,y)\le\delta b_l\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/0/3/2: But the mark of \(x\) is positive.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/0/3/3: This is impossible, since the mark is \(\text{light}(G(x,y)/b_l)\) times the row gate.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/0/4: So the count is at least \(J+1\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/0/5: Since the score is at most \(1\), \((J+1)\,\text{score}\le J+1\le\) count.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/1: Write \(U(y)\) as the conditional average over \(t\) of the average over \(s\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.U_light/2: For each \(t\), \((J+1)\,\mathbb E_s\,\text{score}\le\#\{x:G(x,y)>\delta b_l\}\pi_{b_l}\), using the expected retained count.

decls.name: columns
decls.informal: If \(S\) is admissible, \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions, \(2^i\le P\), \(k<k_*\), \(y\in S\) and \(\gamma(V_{k+1}(y))>0\), then \(\#\{x:G_k(x,y)\ge2\delta f\}\cdot f\le128+4(J+1)\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.columns/2: Use the choice of \(K\) in the constants.

results.informal: For \(D_T=C-E_T+E_TC\): \(D_T\) is nonnegative, strictly forward and substochastic with \(D_T(x,y)\le(T+1)f\) and \(D_T\ge Af\) where \(E_T>0\); if \(g(y)=1\) and \(T\) is admissible then \(D_T(x,y)\le f/256\); and \(C+E_T+E_TC\le(1+2T/A)D_T\).
results.note: These lemmas state the three claims of the paper lemma with \(K_*=T+1\), \(\varepsilon_{\rm good}=1/256\) and \(c_{\rm dom}^{-1}=1+2T/A\).

decls.name: substochastic
decls.informal: If \(f>0\), \(0\le g\le1\) and \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions in \(S'\), then \(D_t=C-E_t+E_tC\) is nonnegative, strictly forward in \(S'\), has \(D_t\mathbf 1\le\mathbf 1\) and \(D_t(x,y)\le(t+1)f\), and \(E_t(x,y)>0\) implies \(D_t(x,y)\ge Af\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.substochastic/1: \(E_t\) satisfies the stage bounds with constant \(t\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.substochastic/8: The second claim is proved; it remains to show the stage bounds for \(D_t\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.substochastic/11/0: Fix \(x,y\) and split on the sign of \(E_t(x,y)\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.substochastic/11/2: If \(E_t(x,y)\ge0\), split on whether it is \(0\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.substochastic/14: A positive entry of \(D_t\) is a positive entry of \(H\), so it is strictly forward in \(S'\).

decls.name: good_col
decls.informal: If \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions, \(0\le g\le1\), \((5/A)^T/T!\le1/1024\) and \(g(y)=1\), then \(D_T(x,y)\le f/256\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.good_col/2: Here \(E_{T+1}(x,y)=fQ(w/f)g(y)\), and the goal is \(w-E_T(x,y)\le f/256\).

decls.name: cover
decls.informal: For every \(T\), \(C(x,y)+E_T(x,y)+(E_TC)(x,y)\le(1+2T/A)\,D_T(x,y)\) where \(D_T=C-E_T+E_TC\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.cover/0: Let \(F=E_T\) and \(D=C-E_T+E_TC\); the goal is \(C+E_T+E_TC\le(1+2T/A)D\) at \((x,y)\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.cover/2: \(D\) satisfies the residual bounds, and \(E_T(x,y)>0\) implies \(D(x,y)\ge Af\).

results.informal: The copied matrix \(C^+(x_i,y_j)=r_i(x)D(x,y)s_j(D(x,y)/f)\) has entries \(\le f/16\), satisfies \(|\mathcal A(C^+)|\le2|\mathcal A(C)|\), and \(C^+P^rv=P^rDv\) for every vector \(v\).
results.note: edge_small, few_nodes and commute are the entry bound \(C^+\le f/q\) with \(q=16\), the active-count bound, and the intertwining \(C^+P^r=P^rD\) (stated on vectors); strict forwardness and substochasticity are the separate lemma newGood.

decls.name: edge_small
decls.informal: If \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions, then every entry of the copied matrix satisfies \(C^+(x',y')\le b_{i+1}\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.edge_small/11/0: Here \(s=1/M\) and \(d\le(k_*+1)f\), so the goal is \(d/M\le f/16\).

decls.name: few_nodes
decls.informal: If \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions and \(2^i\le P\), then \(|\mathcal A(C^+)|\le2|\mathcal A(C)|\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/0: Let \(T=\mathcal A(C)\), \(E\) the set of active vertices (\(V(x)>1/4\)), and \(A'\) the primary copies of \(T\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/1: \(D\) satisfies the residual bounds with support in \(\mathcal A(C)\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/2/0: Write \(C^+(i,j)\) as the product of the three factors, which is positive.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/2/3: Hence each factor is nonzero, and \(D(x,y)>0\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/3/1: The base vertex of \(i\) lies in \(S\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/3/2: \(i\) is the copy of its base vertex with its own index.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/3/3: Consider the outgoing and incoming cases.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/3/4/0: Split on whether \(i\) is the primary copy.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/3/4/1: A primary \(i\) is the primary copy of a vertex of \(\mathcal A(C)\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/3/4/2: A nonprimary \(i\) has \(r_i(x)\ne0\), which forces \(V(x)>1/4\), so \(x\) is active.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/3/5/0: Split on whether \(i\) is the primary copy.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/3/5/1: A primary \(i\) is the primary copy of a column in \(\mathcal A(C)\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.few_nodes/3/5/2: A nonprimary \(i\) with nonzero routing fraction has \(V(x)>1/2\), so \(x\) is active.

decls.name: commute
decls.informal: If \(C\) satisfies the stage conditions, then \((C^+P^rv)(x')=(P^rDv)(x')\) for every vector \(v\) and vertex \(x'\).

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.commute/1/0: With \(f_j=s_j(D(x,y)/f)\), show each term equals \(a\,D(x,y)v(y)f_j\), then sum.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.commute/1/1/2: The term is \(a\,D(x,y)f_j\cdot r_j(y)v(y)\); split on whether \(f_j=0\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.commute/1/1/4: If \(f_j\ne0\) then \(r_j(y)=1\): trivially for \(j=0\), and since \(V(y)>1/2\) otherwise.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.commute/2: Summing over the copies \(y_j\) of all \(y\in S\) gives \((C^+P^rv)(x_i)=a\,(Dv)(x)\).

results.informal: There exist constants \(T,K,J,M\) with \(T>0\), \((5/A)^T/T!\le1/1024\), \((1+32(T+1)/\eta(\delta))\cdot128\le K+1\), \(16(T+1)<M\), and \(64M(T+1)^2\le\delta(J+1)\).
results.note: The Lean constant record fixes \(k_*=T\) first and then \(K\), \(M\) and \(J\) from it, which is the ordering described in the remark.

decls.name: Const
decls.informal: A constant choice is a tuple \((T,K,J,M)\) with \(T>0\), \((5/A)^T/T!\le1/1024\), \((1+32(T+1)/\eta(\delta))\cdot128\le K+1\), \(16(T+1)<M\) and \(64M(T+1)^2\le\delta(J+1)\).

decls.name: exists_const
decls.informal: Such a tuple \((T,K,J,M)\) exists.

results.informal: Correctness (\(C\) a valid stage, \(W\ge0\), \(v\in[0,1]\), \(v=W+Cv\)) is preserved by the update \(W^+=P^r(W+EW)\), \(v^+=P^rv\); after \(k\) stages \(|\mathcal A(C_k)|\le|S|2^k\) and \(0\le v(x)-W_k(\bar x_k)\le|S|2^kb_{i+k}\).
results.note: Correct.raise is the reward identity and update, and finish is the shallow-target bound \(0\le p_0(x)-W_l(\bar x_l)\le|V_0|2^lb_l\) with \(b_l=2^{-4l}\); the choice \(L=O(B)\) is made elsewhere.

decls.name: finish
decls.informal: If \(H\) is correct and \(2^{i+k}\le P\), then \(0\le v(x)-W_k(\bar x_k)\le|S|\,2^k\,b_{i+k}\), where \(\bar x_k\) is the all-primary copy of \(x\) after \(k\) stages.

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.finish/0: Let \(H_k\) be the hierarchy after \(k\) stages and \(y=\bar x_k\); since \(v_k(y)=v(x)\), work with \(v_k(y)\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.finish/5: So \((C_kv_k)(y)\ge0\); now consider the active set \(\mathcal A(C_k)\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.finish/6: \(\mathcal A(C_k)\) is contained in the stage domain.
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.finish/7: \(C_k\) satisfies the stage conditions with support in \(\mathcal A(C_k)\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.finish/9: The restricted sum is at most \(|S|2^kb_{i+k}\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.finish/9/1: Since \(C_k\le b_{i+k}\) and \(v_k\le1\), the sum is at most \(|\mathcal A(C_k)|b_{i+k}\le|S|2^kb_{i+k}\).

decls.name: Correct.raise
decls.informal: If \(H\) is correct, then the next stage \((C^+,\,W^+=P^r(W+EW),\,v^+=P^rv)\) is correct.

chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.Correct.raise/3: \(C^+\) satisfies the stage conditions at rate \(b_{i+1}\).
chunks.ProbabilityHierarchy.Correct.raise/6/4: Evaluate at the base vertex of \(x\).

decls.name: density
decls.informal: If \(H\) is correct and \(2^{i+k}\le P\), then after \(k\) stages \(|\mathcal A(C_k)|\le|S|\,2^k\).
